reviewed_by: Claude review of batched specialist routing actions
reason: The mission specialist loop in src/nebula/v3/agent_tooling.py accepted exactly one routing action per provider response and raised "specialist must request exactly one sequential routing action" on anything else, so a model that batched independent actions lost the whole task; OpenRouter routes cannot honour parallel_tool_calls=false, so batching reaches Core in practice. A routing response may now carry several actions: _routing_batch validates the whole response first (prose, empty response, repeated call ids, unavailable tools), then the specialist brokers the calls one at a time, in order, each with its own durable invocation, idempotency key, budget slot and approval. src/nebula/v3/orchestration.py gains the matching mission-side pieces: SpecialistApprovalRequired carries the calls a paused batch already completed, MissionRuntime._dispatch persists that partial turn and its tokens, cost and tool-call count before pausing, call_records reads either turn shape, and _model_safe_specialist_result sanitizes every call in a batch rather than only the first. tests/v3/test_specialist_tool_batches.py is new and covers both files end to end; tests/v3/test_missions.py, tests/v3/test_approval_continuation.py and tests/v3/test_approval_handoff.py are the suites that drive mission turns and the approval checkpoint this change touches.
exclusions: No frontend, native or Playwright change: missions emit the same task, attempt and approval records, and no ui/src file is touched. tests/v3/test_orchestration.py is deliberately not selected: two of its tests (test_mission_compacts_only_model_facing_dependency_context_and_charges_usage and test_mission_rejects_compaction_before_call_when_budget_is_insufficient) fail identically on pristine origin/main, where a 600-token stub context window now trips the context-capacity rejection in ContextService._hierarchical_memory ("model context leaves too little room for a faithful compaction summary", a FAILED task) before the token-budget rejection the tests assert ("insufficient mission token budget", a BLOCKED task). That rot predates this branch (COMPACTOR_MIN_OUTPUT_TOKENS changed in #332) and belongs to context compaction, not to this change; the rest of that file passes on this branch. The orchestration paths this branch does touch are covered by the new file, which runs a full MissionRuntime through a batched approval pause and resume. No live mission was run: the specialist loop is exercised here with a scripted provider and a recording broker, which is the only way to pin call order, per-call idempotency keys and the partial-result hand-off deterministically.
